subject: Handback/export lifecycle for audit & access logs — playbook questions
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <security@finvero.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: LogOps Team <logops@globex.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on handback of audit/access logs & deletion proof

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this. We are working through our compliance checklist for a scheduled handback and have a few specific questions about Redwood's capabilities for audit + access logs:

- What are the supported export formats (ndjson, parquet, syslog, etc.) and is there a recommended format for downstream ingestion into our SIEM?
- Typical delivery SLA for an ad-hoc handback (full tenant audit logs for 90 days)? Any chunking/streaming options?
- Do exports include cryptographic checksums (e.g. SHA256) and a signed attestation so we can prove integrity to our auditors?
- How does Redwood handle deletion evidence once we request data erase (tombstone vs physical removal)? Can you provide a certificate or timestamped manifest?
- Cross-border: we need to know if exports can be restricted to EU-only storage/encryption keys before transit.
- Is there an option to request an incremental snapshot cadence (daily diffs) versus a complete dump?

We'll need a sample manifest and a short playbook we can give our legal/compliance teams. Attaching our internal template — please advise if that's feasible and what the expected timeline would be.

Appreciate a concise reply and any sample artifacts you can attach.

Best,
Marta
Security Operations Lead
Finvero Health

Attachment: finvero_handback_template.xlsx (referenced)

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <security@finvero.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on handback of audit/access logs & deletion proof

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below and I attached a concise export spec and a sample manifest for a 90-day handback. If you'd like, we can run through this on a short call to confirm formats for your SIEM.

Quick answers:
- Supported formats: ndjson (line-delimited JSON) and compressed Parquet for bulk analytics; syslog stream for real-time ingestion. Our recommendation for SIEM ingestion is ndjson (one event per line) gzipped.

- Delivery SLA / cadence: For an ad‑hoc full tenant 90‑day export we target 5–7 business days for a standard export (subject to rate limits and data volume). We offer chunked exports (default 10GB chunks) and a streaming S3-compatible endpoint if you want to start ingesting while the export runs.

- Integrity proof: Exports include a manifest.csv with per-file SHA256 checksums plus a signed attestation (PKCS#7) from Redwood's export service. The signed attestation contains an export timestamp, tenant id, and checksum list.

- Deletion evidence: Two parts — (1) export/handback: we produce an export manifest and attestation as above; (2) deletion inside Redwood: for hosted tenants we maintain a tombstone+erasure workflow. After you request erase, we timestamp the tombstone, remove logical pointers, and then schedule physical overwrite according to the retention/erase window. We provide a deletion certificate (signed, timestamped) showing the tombstone and final erase date when the job completes.

- Cross-border / key control: For EU-only exports we can route the export to an EU S3 endpoint and encrypt with a customer-managed key (CMK) in your EU KMS. For Private deployments, exports never leave your VPC unless you grant egress.

- Incremental snapshots: Yes — daily diffs (ndjson deltas) are available. We can also provide a rolling snapshot that includes sequence tokens for resume/confirmation.

Attachments: finvero_export_spec.pdf (format, chunking, encryption), sample_manifest_20280315.csv (example manifest + checksums).

Next steps: If the spec looks good, pick either (A) ad-hoc full export (we'll open a support job) or (B) set up a streaming S3 endpoint for phased ingestion. We can run a 30‑minute runbook walkthrough.

--
Avery Johnson
Product Security (Redwood Inference)

Marta — adding a couple of contractual/assurance notes from Legal & Compliance:

- Retention windows: Standard hosted retention is 365 days for audit trails unless an enterprise contract specifies otherwise. We can support shorter (30/90 days) or longer (multi‑year) retention in Dedicated/Private with contract language.

- Deletion certification: We provide a deletion certificate that includes (i) export manifest id, (ii) tombstone timestamp, (iii) wipe completion timestamp, and (iv) signed statement by Redwood's compliance officer. For high‑assurance requests we can route the final erase through an HSM-backed KMS so the key destruction path is auditable.

- SLA exceptions & hold requests: If you anticipate a legal hold, inform us as soon as possible. Legal holds will prevent automated erasure; they'll require a signed form and may extend export timelines.

- Audit support: We can produce a sample attestation and have our compliance engineer join an evidence review call. Note that any PII in the logs can be redacted on request prior to export — we have a standard redaction playbook but recommend keeping raw exports for forensic teams unless otherwise required.

I'll coordinate the deletion certificate template and drop it into the Drive link Avery mentioned.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Compliance & Legal
Redwood Inference
